headline: New evening confusion since about mid-October, including the stove left on, and a caregiver asking for respite on Nov 22. The follow-up work-up isn't documented yet.

items.statement: On 2026-11-02, Robert reported about two weeks of increased evening confusion, with the stove left on once. Jerónimo was oriented to person and place but not date, and had no fever. The nurse planned a urinalysis, medication review and PCP visit that week. The notes and encounter record show no results or visit after that date.
items.verifier_note: All facts match the 11-02 nursing note: two weeks of evening confusion, stove left on once, oriented to person and place but not date, no fever, and the plan for urinalysis, medication review and a PCP visit that week. The encounters record is empty, so it shows no later results or visit.

items.statement: On 2026-11-22, Robert (grandson and primary caregiver) reported exhaustion and poor sleep. He is worried about managing evenings alone and requested respite. The social worker discussed respite options and a caregiver support group. This overlaps with the evening confusion reported on Nov 2.
items.verifier_note: The 11-22 social work note matches every detail in the statement. The 11-02 nursing note reports evening confusion, so the overlap claim is also supported.

items.statement: No influenza vaccine is recorded this season (season start 2026-08-01). The most recent dose was on 2026-06-30, before the season began.
items.verifier_note: The record shows flu_vaccine_this_season is false and the season started 2026-08-01. The most recent dose was 2026-06-30, which is before the season start.

questions_for_team: Were the urinalysis, medication review and PCP visit planned on Nov 2 completed? What did they show, and who is following up on the evening confusion?
What interim safety measures are needed for the stove and for evenings, given the confusion and Robert's report that he is exhausted?
Which respite options can start now, and who will follow up with Robert after the Nov 22 meeting?
The fall entry of Sep 25 was corrected as a charting error. Does the PT evaluation of Sep 29, which was based on that fall, need to be re-verified or closed out?
Should the influenza vaccine be offered this season?

checks: Confirm the review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) and identify what changed since the last IDT review, using the enrollment date 2024-04-21 as the baseline if no prior review is documented.

Ischemic heart disease (onset 2026-06-30): review cardiac events in the window, including chest pain or angina episodes, nitroglycerin spray use frequency, ED visits, urgent care contacts, admissions, and any cardiology follow-up or testing that is scheduled or completed.

Medication changes since the last review: verify start and stop dates for metoprolol succinate, clopidogrel, nitroglycerin spray, simvastatin, and alendronic acid (all started June to July 2026). Check adherence, missed doses, refill gaps, and any dose changes or new prescriptions from outside prescribers.

Bleeding and antiplatelet safety: because clopidogrel is active alongside other medications, screen the window for bleeding events, GI bleeding, bruising, epistaxis, and any dental or procedural bleeding concerns, and flag for prescriber review as appropriate.
Heart rate and blood pressure trend on metoprolol: review recorded HR and BP values, dizziness, orthostatic symptoms, fatigue, and any falls, and flag readings outside the team's agreed thresholds.

Falls and fracture risk: review any falls, near-falls, or fractures in the window. Given osteoporosis (2023) and scoliosis, check the bone-health plan, alendronic acid administration instructions (upright positioning, fasting), dental status, and whether follow-up bone density or calcium/vitamin D status is documented as due.

Substance use (dependent drug abuse, onset 2018): review the window for relapse signals, opioid or other controlled-substance prescriptions and refill pattern, early refill requests, pharmacy or prescriber changes, withdrawal or craving reports, and naloxone availability. Confirm whether any current prescriptions for pain or migraine medicines are being monitored under the care plan.

Chronic pain and chronic intractable migraine: review pain scores, migraine frequency and days per month, acute medication use, headache-related ED visits, and whether the pain plan has been updated since the last review. Check for interactions between pain or migraine treatments and the new cardiac medications.

Obesity (BMI 30+): review weight trend and BMI over the window, dietary and activity goals, and any nutrition or exercise referrals. Consider cardiac rehab eligibility as a discussion item for the team, not a recommendation.

Dental and oral health (impacted molars, onset 1991): check whether dental extraction or treatment is scheduled, pending, or completed, and whether any dental procedure requires coordination with antiplatelet therapy and alendronate for the prescriber to review.

Function, ADLs, cognition, mood, and social supports: review ADL and IADL changes, mobility and assistive device use, cognitive screening results, depression or anxiety screening (including post-cardiac event mood), IDT or program attendance, caregiver or social support changes, and any transportation or housing barriers. Confirm the care plan items due in the window, including reassessments and goal reviews.

Allergies: the record lists no allergies. Confirm this with the participant and pharmacy since multiple new medications were started. Summarize all findings in a brief for the IDT, flagging items for clinician decision rather than making treatment recommendations.
